title: Moving Americans Privacy Protection Act
official_summary:
Moving Americans Privacy Protection Act

This act revises requirements regarding the public disclosure of personally identifiable information contained in the manifest of vessels or aircraft entering a U.S. port or place. Specifically, the act directs U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to remove such information, including Social Security numbers and passport numbers, from a manifest signed and transmitted to CBP before it is accessible by the public.

summary.headline: New law requires Customs and Border Protection to remove personal details like Social Security and passport numbers from public shipping manifests.
summary.what_it_does: Ships and aircraft entering the U.S. must send a manifest, a list of what they carry, to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Some of this manifest information can be made public. This law directs CBP to remove personally identifiable information, such as Social Security numbers and passport numbers, from these manifests before the public can see them.

who_it_affects.group: People moving household goods to the U.S. from abroad, such as returning military members and overseas workers
who_it_affects.how: Their Social Security numbers, passport numbers, and similar personal details listed on shipping manifests must be removed before the records are made public.
The agency must strip personal identifying information from manifests before making them publicly accessible.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 9, 2024; the summary does not give a separate start date.
